# Appeal Letter

**Governing Policy:** Cohere Health: Avera Commercial Guidelines index (Knee Arthroplasty v8, Knee Arthroscopy v10, Hip Arthroplasty v5, Hip Arthroscopy v6, Shoulder Arthroplasty v4, Shoulder Arthroscopy v5, Open Shoulder v4, Cervical Spinal Fusion v5, Lumbar Spinal Fusion v3, Spinal Decompression v4.1, Ankle Arthroplasty v4, Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3)
URL: https://help.coherehealth.com/payer-info/en/articles/13602157-avera-health-plan-commercial-guidelines

---

**RE: Appeal of Denial — Bunion Surgery (CPT 28296)**
Member: Quinn Delgado
Member ID: W570305899
Denial date: 2026-08-17
Reference number: POC-A389519C6D-33639
Payer/Plan: Avera Health Plans (Commercial/ACA), South Dakota

Dear Avera Health Plans Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for bunion surgery (hallux valgus correction, CPT 28296), which was denied on 2026-08-17 as not medically necessary. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I am asking the plan to reconsider its decision.

## Why I Am Appealing

The denial notice states that my requested procedure "does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity," and points generally to the plan's clinical review criteria under the Great Toe Surgical Treatments guideline. However, the plan documents made available to me for this appeal are limited to the following:

- "All Collections Review Criteria Avera Health Plan Avera Health Plan:"
- "Commercial & Medicare Advantage Attachment icon Xenograft Implantation (Single Service).pdf Attachment icon Site of Service Criteria for Inpatient vs."
- "Commercial/Medicaid & Medicare Advantage Guidelines Review Criteria:"

These are index and document-title fragments. They do not contain the specific clinical thresholds (for example, angle measurements, symptom duration, or conservative-care requirements) that the plan actually applied to decide my case. Because I have not been given the specific criteria language, I am not able to show point-by-point how my records meet it — and I want to be transparent that I am not quoting policy criteria here because none were provided to me. I am respectfully asking the plan to identify, in writing, the exact criteria from the Great Toe Surgical Treatments guideline used to evaluate my request, along with the specific reasons my records were found not to meet them.

## What My Records Show

While I wait for the plan to identify the specific criteria it applied, I want the following facts from my medical record to be part of the appeal file:

- **Duration and severity of symptoms:** 18 months of progressive foot pain that is not relieved by rest.
- **Conservative treatment completed:** Activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic over 12 weeks (2026-04-02 to 2026-06-25), with 20 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging findings:** Weight-bearing foot radiographs on 2026-06-07 showed a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.
- **Functional impact:** I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and there is documented ulceration risk over the bony prominence.
- **Exam findings:** Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- **No disqualifying factors noted in the record:** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

These findings are documented in the prior authorization packet submitted by my surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, who has determined that surgery is medically necessary for my condition.

## My Request

I ask that the plan:

1. Reconsider the denial of CPT 28296 in light of the clinical findings above; and
2. Provide the specific medical necessity criteria from the Great Toe Surgical Treatments guideline that were applied to my case, so that I and my surgeon can respond directly to any remaining concerns.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-02-13** (180 days from the date of the denial notice). I will send this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, or, if that is not available, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for your time and reconsideration.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Quinn Delgado
Member ID: W570305899
[Address]
[Phone number]
[Email address]
Date: [Date of signing]

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
